title: Bias Audit Scores Disagree on Model Ranking Across Ten Instruments
plain: A study ran ten extrinsic bias audit instruments over a shared panel of ten frontier language models through a single pooled inference gateway, testing occupational gender bias and then replicating on age and socioeconomic status. Eight of the ten tools detected bias with confidence intervals clear of zero, but cross-t

angles.claim: A single bias audit score used to certify or rank vendors during procurement is not valid evidence, regardless of which tool produced it.
angles.audience: AI governance and procurement leads inside utilities certifying vendor models for fairness compliance
angles.rank_reason: Directly changes a procurement and compliance decision: certification on one instrument must stop, and the study's own concordance test (W=0.07) supports this without extrapolation.

angles.claim: Detection and ranking are separate claims, so a tool that reliably flags bias cannot be trusted to say which of two models is fairer.
angles.audience: Engineers building or selecting bias evaluation pipelines for production model governance
angles.rank_reason: Gives engineers a concrete Monday check (does our pipeline conflate detection with ranking) but is narrower than the procurement-level decision above.

angles.claim: Audit format, not just tool choice, determines the direction of a bias finding, so switching from forced-choice to free-generation testing can flip the reported bias.
angles.audience: Teams designing or auditing bias test suites who must choose which instrument format to standardize on
angles.rank_reason: Actionable and specific to the study's format-split finding, but it informs a technical design choice rather than a governance or procurement decision, so it ranks last.
